messages:
anya: Hi all — first week, first real PR. Quick sanity check: branching name, commit style, and reviewer etiquette?
samir: Welcome! Branch pattern: feat/<ticket>-short-desc or fix/<ticket>-desc. Lowercase, hyphens.
meera: Commits: follow Conventional Commits. Keep each PR focused; we squash on merge so aim for one logical commit.
anya: Good to know. Who should I add as reviewers for a serving-runtime change that touches config?
meera: Check CODEOWNERS first. Likely @eng-runtime and @eng-platform. If it touches infra-level configs, add @eng-infra and ping @kevin.
kevin: For anything that could change startup behavior or rollout safety, require 2 reviewers incl. one senior. Small tweaks can be single-review.
samir: PR body checklist: summary, issue link, test steps, backward-compat notes, migration instructions if any. Our bot enforces a checklist.
anya: CI failed locally on linting. Any quick steps to run checks before pushing?
meera: Run `./scripts/bootstrap` then `./scripts/lint` and `./scripts/test-local --fast`. Fix lint/mypy locally — faster than CI loops.
anyA: (typo) — meant: thanks! :)
devx-bot: Tip: mark WIP PRs as Draft. Use labels added by autolabeler. For flakey tests, tag `flaky` and add a note in the PR.
kevin: One more rule: split large refactors into a short RFC/ADR first or smaller incremental PRs. Review bandwidth is limited.
anya: I’ll open as Draft and tag reviewers once ready. Could someone pair-review before I tilt to final?
meera: Happy to pair-review — DM me and we can do a quick walkthrough.
